title: Rocket Report: China wants a Raptor 3 engine; SpaceX set for big Starship test
gist: SpaceX's Falcon 9 has become so oversubscribed it is turning away commercial customers (benefiting Europe's Avio), while United Launch Alliance's expendable-rocket model fades toward irrelevance; meanwhile China's commercial launch sector is maturing fast and a Chinese startup has unveiled an engine nearly identical to SpaceX's Raptor 3.

themes.theme: SpaceX capacity constraints reshape the market

insights.claim: SpaceX has stopped accepting new orders for commercial Falcon 9 launches for multiple prospective customers, effectively going 'captive' to existing commitments and pushing spillover demand to competitors like Italy's Avio.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: A supply-constrained Falcon 9 is a structural tailwind for alternative launch providers (Avio, ULA, new entrants) gaining pricing power and backlog even without matching SpaceX's cost structure.
insights.quote: SpaceX has already gone captive because we have a whole bunch of customers coming to us and saying, ‘Oh my God, can you fly us?’
insights.locator: Avio seeks to cash in on Falcon 9 retreat

insights.claim: Turned-away SpaceX customers are lobbying European institutions at events like the International Space Summit in Paris for subsidies to offset the higher cost of flying on Europe's Vega C rocket.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Potential EU launch subsidies would be a policy-driven demand signal for Avio and other European launch suppliers, worth monitoring for procurement/appropriations news.
insights.locator: Europe’s answer to this, a subsidy?

insights.claim: The author argues that subsidizing launches on expendable rockets like Vega C is a poor policy choice, and Europe should instead direct investment toward developers of reusable, more cost-competitive launch vehicles.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: A contrarian editorial view against expendable-rocket subsidies flags political/industrial risk for Avio's long-term competitiveness even if it captures near-term overflow demand.
insights.quote: In our view, subsidizing launches on expendable launch technology is a poor plan.
insights.locator: In our view, subsidizing launches on expendable launch technology

insights.claim: SpaceX's Falcon rocket family reached its 700th launch (687 Falcon 9, 13 Falcon Heavy) with the mPOWER-F mission for SES, and booster B1080 completed its 29th flight, underscoring SpaceX's reusability-driven cadence advantage.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Booster reuse at this scale (29 flights on one core) is the cost/cadence moat competitors like ULA, Avio, and Chinese entrants still cannot match.

insights.claim: United Launch Alliance, co-owned by Boeing and Lockheed Martin, is nearly alone among major US launch companies in not embracing reusability and vehicle-family diversification, leaving its business model increasingly outdated two decades after its founding.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: ULA's single-architecture, expendable strategy is a structural competitive disadvantage; a sale or strategic pivot is increasingly likely and worth tracking for M&A activity.
insights.locator: What does the future hold for United Launch Alliance?

insights.claim: ULA's new Vulcan rocket has been delayed by problems with its solid rocket boosters but could return to flight by the end of the month with a commercial Amazon satellite launch, even as the company's finances worsen and it seeks additional funding.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: ULA's need for outside capital signals its parent companies (Boeing, Lockheed) may divest; a new owner willing to invest in new tech is framed as its only long-term viability path.

insights.claim: China conducted four rocket launches within 44 hours across multiple spaceports, with three of the four missions flown by commercial or quasi-commercial entities rather than the traditional state Long March fleet.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: China's commercial launch sector is shifting from test flights to operational cadence, meaning future satellite-constellation buildouts there will no longer depend solely on state rockets — a capacity signal for Western competitors.
insights.locator: China launches four rockets in two days

insights.claim: Chinese startup Space Pioneer, which has raised nearly $1 billion, unveiled a new Tianhuo-21 methane-liquid oxygen engine whose design and thrust (2,450 kN at sea level) closely mirror SpaceX's Raptor 3 engine.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Well-capitalized Chinese startups are visibly converging on SpaceX's engine architecture, a leading indicator of intensifying Sino-American competition in reusable heavy-lift launch.
insights.locator: Chinese space company reveals Raptor 3-like engine design

insights.claim: Elon Musk publicly cast doubt on how easily a new company could replicate the Raptor 3 engine, citing its complex internal geometry that requires highly modified 3D metal printing to manufacture despite its visually simple exterior.
insights.speaker: Elon Musk (quoted)
insights.so_what: Musk's skepticism suggests SpaceX's true moat is manufacturing process/tooling rather than visible design, meaning apparent lookalike engines may still lag years behind in reliability and production yield.
insights.quote: While it appears simple on the outside (necessary to survive extreme heat without a heat shield), the inside has very complex geometry that can only be manufactured using highly modified 3D metal printing.
insights.locator: Would it be difficult to replicate?

insights.claim: NASA selected Blue Origin over Rocket Lab to develop, launch, and operate a $700 million Mars Telecommunications Network spacecraft, and Rocket Lab formally protested the decision to the US Government Accountability Office.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: A GAO protest introduces schedule risk to a $700M NASA award; contractors and investors should watch for a ruling that could delay or reverse Blue Origin's contract.
insights.locator: Two launch companies spar over Mars mission

insights.claim: Rocket Lab's protest alleges NASA's technical review of its proposal was inconsistent and contained incorrect assertions, while Blue Origin warns the protest could delay the mission's targeted 2028 launch.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: A protracted procurement fight raises execution risk for a 2028 Mars comms mission and signals sharpening competitive tension between Blue Origin and Rocket Lab for government contracts.
insights.quote: The agency’s punitive review of Rocket Lab’s technical volume was inconsistent, making incorrect assertions and conclusions,

insights.claim: SpaceX targeted its 14th Starship mission for as early as September 22 (later slipping to September 28) as the first attempt to fly the vehicle into orbit, carrying 26 of the larger V3 Starlink satellites to a 275 km orbit and planning six orbits over roughly 10 hours.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: A successful first orbital Starship flight would be a major milestone for SpaceX's heavy-lift and Starlink V3 deployment capacity, worth watching given the vehicle's history of schedule slips since its April 2023 debut.
insights.locator: SpaceX set for first Starship orbital flight

insights.claim: NASA's $4.3 billion Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, launched on a Falcon Heavy, achieved such a precise trajectory that its fuel load is now expected to last 22 years — more than double the original minimum five-year (plus five-year extension) mission plan.
insights.speaker: Jamie Dunn (quoted)
insights.so_what: Precision launch execution by SpaceX directly extended a $4.3B science asset's operational life by over a decade, a tangible reliability data point for Falcon Heavy's value proposition on high-value payloads.
insights.quote: As a result of exquisite planning by our orbital dynamics team, brilliant execution by the operations team, and a precise launch from SpaceX, Roman has fuel for at least 22 years of potential science operations,
insights.locator: Falcon Heavy nailed Roman telescope’s launch

insights.claim: French startup Sirius Space Services completed the first full-system hot-fire test of its STAR-1 engine (55 kN thrust, liquid oxygen/methane), validating integrated operation of its turbopumps, combustion chamber, injector plate, avionics, and software for the first time.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: A new European methalox engine reaching integrated hot-fire is an early-stage signal of a broader European launch-vehicle family (nine STAR-1 engines per core stage) that could compete for future European launch demand.
insights.locator: French company test-fires new rocket engine

insights.claim: Blue Origin expanded a public-private partnership with the Air Force Research Laboratory to study oxygen-rich and full-flow staged combustion propulsion technologies, while also continuing to develop its BE-7 lunar-lander engine.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Robertson (quoted)
insights.so_what: Government-funded propulsion R&D partnerships give Blue Origin access to historic full-flow staged combustion research, potentially accelerating next-gen engine development relevant to its lunar and orbital programs.
insights.locator: Blue Origin studying full-flow staged combustion

insights.claim: A Vega C rocket successfully launched ESA's FLEX Earth Explorer and Copernicus Sentinel-3C satellites together using a new dual-satellite adapter called Vespa, only the second Vega launch of the year.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: New dual-payload adapter technology improves Vega C's per-launch economics, relevant to its competitiveness as it absorbs overflow demand from SpaceX.
insights.locator: Vega C successfully lofts two satellites
